items.prose: Laboratory quality assurance on virgin steam-activated coconut shell carbon confirmed an exceptional iodine number of 1,150 mg/g and surface area of 1,200 m²/g. The predominantly microporous structure demonstrated near-total removal of trace volatile radionuclides.

After eight months of treating groundwater contaminated by a machine shop degreaser leak, the mass transfer zone reached the bed exit. Effluent trichloroethylene (TCE) jumped from nondetect to 24 ppb, signaling the need for immediate carbon replacement.

Optimizing backwash water rate achieved a 35% fluidized bed expansion, scrubbing accumulated clay particles without overflowing 12x40 mesh carbon granules. Carbon mechanical attrition loss was held to less than 1.5% per annum.

Passing spent carbon through a direct-fired rotary kiln at 850°C under an injected steam blanket pyrolyzed and volatilized all adsorbed organic poisons. The reactivated carbon regained 92% of its virgin iodine number with only 6% total volume loss.

Heavy 20-minute empty-bed contact time allowed the GAC vessel to physically retard dissolved Radon-222 gas transit. By the time water exited the carbon bed, the 3.8-day half-life of radon had elapsed, reducing radioactivity in drinking water by 98%.

Cyanobacterial blooms in the emergency surface reservoir released geosmin and 2-methylisoborneol (2-MIB), giving water a foul musty, earthy taste. A single pass through mesoporous wood-based GAC stripped both compounds below human olfactory thresholds (<5 ng/L).

Following ozone oxidation, biodegradable organic carbon fed dense colonies of aerobic nitrifying bacteria inside the macropores of the GAC bed. The biological action continually self-regenerated adsorption sites, extending physical carbon bed life past five years.
